mappings.note: Glosses the Rajasthani word 'भीर' (= विपत्ति). The deliverable is the poet's diction, i.e. कला-पक्ष, so LO-5 rather than LO-4 -- nothing in the pad's content or narrative has to be recalled to answer it.
Recalls the Draupadi allusion the first pad makes (चीर बढ़ाकर). Content comprehension of the prescribed poem = LO-4; LO-5 would be wrong because no भाव or कला term is being explained.
What Meera petitions Krishna for -- straight काव्यबोध on the first pad. LO-4 and not LO-5: the answer is the pad's stated request, not an interpretation of its feeling.
The identifying mark of her आराध्य (मोर मुकुट) as the pad states it. Factual recall from the poem, hence LO-4 rather than the कला-पक्ष outcome LO-5.
Her prayer to be made a सेविका -- the content of the second pad. LO-4; LO-5 is reserved here for items that ask for a gloss or for भाव/कला to be named.
Asks the आशय of the line 'चाकर रहस्यूँ, बाग लगास्यूँ...'. Paraphrasing a poetic line is भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या, so LO-5 rather than LO-4's content recall.
Where she wishes to sing Krishna's लीलाएँ (वृंदावन की कुंज गलियाँ). A place named in the pad, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
Which जागीर the चाकरी earns her (भक्ति). The pad names the reward, so this is comprehension (LO-4), not an explanation of the metaphor's craft (LO-5).
Gloss of the compound 'मोर मुगट'. Word-level explanation of the poet's language = कला-पक्ष, so LO-5; LO-4 covers what the pad says, not how it says it.
Which garland Krishna wears (वैजयंती). Detail stated in the pad -- LO-4, not LO-5.
Why she wants a 'बारी' between the palaces -- a reason the pad itself supplies (to see Krishna). LO-4; no भाव or कला term is asked to be explained, so not LO-5.
Gloss of 'कुसुम्बी' (deep red). Diction of the poem, hence the कला-पक्ष outcome LO-5 rather than LO-4.
What she prays for -- darshan at the Yamuna bank at midnight. Content of the pad, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What Meera wants of Krishna (दर्शन). Comprehension item, LO-4; LO-5 would misdescribe it as a भाव/कला explanation.

Why her heart is अधीर -- the reason is stated in the pad (longing to meet Krishna). Answerable as content, so LO-4 rather than LO-5, which is kept for items that ask the भाव to be named or a line to be construed.
What she wants placed among the palaces (झरोखा). A detail of the pad, LO-4 and not LO-5.
How her भक्ति-भाव will grow -- by living near Krishna, as the pad says. Content comprehension (LO-4), not an explanation of the कला-पक्ष (LO-5).
Asks the तात्पर्य of 'सुमरण पास्यूँ खरची' -- construing the wages/remembrance metaphor. That is भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या (LO-5), not recall (LO-4).
At what hour she wants darshan (आधी रात). Time stated in the pad -- LO-4, not LO-5.
Asks how the poet has depicted Krishna's रूप-सौंदर्य (पीताम्बर, मनमोहक). The deliverable is the manner of the description, i.e. कला-पक्ष -- LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Meaning of the Rajasthani line 'स्याम म्हाने चाकर राखो जी'. A construal of the poet's own words, so LO-5; LO-4 would fit only if the pad's content were being recalled.
Meaning of 'हिवड़ो घणो अधीराँ'. Dialect line gloss = कला-पक्ष/भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या (LO-5), not content recall (LO-4).
Biographical: whose kingdom Meera married into (मेवाड़). Neither LO covers कवि-परिचय -- LO-4 is poem comprehension and LO-5 is भाव/कला -- so the honest citation is the literature competency itself.
Why Meera settled in Vrindavan -- a fact of her life, not of the two prescribed pads. Competency-level C-H2.3 because no LO in this thin set covers poet biography.
Why, in the second pad, she wants Shyam's चाकरी (to stay near him). Comprehension of the prescribed poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Whom the first pad petitions (कृष्ण). Content recall from the named pad, hence LO-4.
Which जागीर she seeks (कृष्ण की भक्ति). The pad states it, so LO-4 rather than an interpretive LO-5 reading.
Date and place of Meera's birth. Pure कवि-परिचय; cited at competency level because neither LO-4 nor LO-5 reaches beyond the poem text.
Age at marriage -- biography again. C-H2.3 rather than LO-4, which is confined to काव्यबोध on the prescribed pads.
Name of Meera's guru (संत रैदास). Literary-historical fact about the poet, so the competency, not the poem-bound LOs.
Whom Meera married (कुंवर भोजराज). Biography, mapped to C-H2.3 for the same reason as the other कवि-परिचय items.
Asks which भाव her भक्ति belongs to (दैन्य और माधुर्य). Naming the emotive register is exactly भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
Where she went after leaving home (वृंदावन) -- asked as a fact of her life, not as something the pads state. C-H2.3 rather than LO-4.
What she wants to sing in Vrindavan's lanes (कृष्ण लीला) -- stated in the second pad. LO-4, not the biographical competency, because the answer comes from the poem.
How many of Meera's काव्य-कृतियाँ survive. A bibliographic fact about the poet's corpus; no LO covers it, so C-H2.3.
Asks the भावार्थ of 'तीनूं बातां सरसी'. Explicitly an explanation of the line's भाव-पक्ष -- LO-5, not LO-4.
तात्पर्य of 'काटी कुंजर पीर'. Construing the Gajendra allusion as phrased by the poet is भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या (LO-5); the bare fact of the allusion would have been LO-4.
What she would spend her wages on (कृष्ण का स्मरण). The pad supplies it, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.

Whose darshan she wants each morning (कृष्ण). Content of the second pad = LO-4. (Stem carries a wrapped option list and the printed option labels do not match the answer -- mapped on content as instructed.)
Who removes people's suffering (ईश्वर) -- the first pad's governing idea, answerable from it. LO-4; LO-5 is not right because no भाव is asked to be named or line construed.
What Meera wants to become (सेविका). Direct comprehension of the second pad, hence LO-4.
What Krishna extended to protect Draupadi (वस्त्र) -- the allusion the first pad makes. LO-4, not LO-5.
What she would plant as a maid (बाग). Stated in the pad, so LO-4 rather than the interpretive LO-5.
Which crown Krishna wears (मोर पंख). Content recall from the pad; LO-5 is reserved for glosses like 'मोर मुगट' का तात्पर्य, which this is not.
Which colour sari she would wear (कुसुंबी). Asked as a fact of the pad, unlike the separate item that asks the meaning of 'कुसुम्बी' -- that one is LO-5, this one LO-4.
Where Krishna grazes cattle (वृंदावन). Comprehension detail, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Where she seeks midnight darshan (यमुना किनारे). Place named in the pad, so LO-4.
Which form God took to save Prahlad (नृसिंह) -- one of the first pad's three भक्त-रक्षा allusions. LO-4; nothing about the poem's craft is asked, so not LO-5.
Which devotees Meera invokes to have her pain removed (द्रौपदी, प्रहलाद, हाथी). The pad's list, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Why she wants to plant a garden as a servant -- reason supplied by the pad (daily darshan). LO-4, not LO-5.
Which garland Krishna wears (वैजयंती). Duplicate-in-substance of an earlier recall item and mapped the same way: LO-4, not LO-5.
How the first pad frames the plea to remove her pain -- by citing the devotees God has already helped. The answer is the pad's own argument, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.

How the आराध्य is conceived in her poetry (सगुण साकार गोपी-वल्लभ). That is a statement about the poetry's भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5; C-H2.3 would be right only if it asked about her life rather than her verse.
Whom the pads are addressed to (अपने आराध्य). Answerable from the poems themselves, hence LO-4 rather than the biographical competency.
Which languages Meera is reckoned a poet of. This is her standing in literary history, not the language of the two prescribed pads, so C-H2.3 rather than LO-5.
Whose disciple Meera was (संत रैदास). Biography, so the competency; LO-4/LO-5 are both confined to the prescribed pads.

Which languages are mixed in the पद themselves (राजस्थानी, ब्रज, गुजराती). A statement about the poems' language = कला-पक्ष, so LO-5 -- and unlike the sibling item about her standing as a poet, which is C-H2.3.
Whom Krishna took the नृसिंह form to save. The pad's allusion, recalled as content -- LO-4, not LO-5.
Asks for comment on Meera's भाषा-शैली (सरल, सहज, बोलचाल). Style is the कला-पक्ष, so LO-5; LO-4 would claim content comprehension that this item never tests.
What Meera is willing to do to reach Krishna (all of: garden, palace, servitude). A summary of the second pad's content, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
